newsitem.title: POLAND: Zloty edges higher vs basket as Kolodko quits.
newsitem.headline: Zloty edges higher vs basket as Kolodko quits.

text.p: The Polish zloty ventured higher against the basket of currencies in late trade as banks closed long currency positions opened this morning in anticipation of a zloty decline after Finance Minister Grzegorz Kolodko quit.
But the zloty held its ground and financial markets kept their composure while largely unkonwn Marek Bulka was appointed Kolodko's succesor.

"Some opened currency positions thinking the zloty would fall, but after a while it became apparant this would not happen today and banks started to close positions, pulling the zloty higher," said Piotr Czyzewski of ING Bank in Warsaw.
Dealers were mixed on whether the zloty would probe higher ground on Wednesday, uncertain about central bank interventions if the unit broke resistance at 2.5 percent from parity.
The zloty closed at 2.54/2.48 percent from the trading band centre, stronger that Monday's 2.43/2.36 percent close.
It was at 3.0025/40 to the dollar, up from 3.0125/45 on Monday and at 1.8285/95 to the mark, flat from 1.8288/02.

New finance chief Belka reassured markets that he would continue a policy of macroecnomic consolidation, curbing inflation and keeping a tight budget, but some analysts said investors may be cautious until they see him in action.

The Polish money market remained hampered by small liquidity as banks entered the monthly required reserve period with low levels and treasury bill and bond payments further reduced free-cash this week, dealers said.
Overnight rates close at 23.05/23.55 percent against opening's 22.65/22.85, while tomorrow/next were at 23.25/23.85 from 22.50/23.50 percent.
Dealers said some banks sold treasury- and NBP-bills in secondary trade to gain liquidity, which was expected to return to the market by the end of the week.
